node-1.label: A 74-year-old man presented with a tender, enlarging scalp lesion of 6 months' duration

node-2.label: The patient has a history of multiple squamous cell carcinomas treated with Mohs micrographic surgery

node-3.label: Skin examination revealed a 5-mm bright pink, dome-shaped papule with overlying vessels at the crown of the scalp, with no purulent discharge or overlying skin changes

why.why: Pathologist analysis reinforces that the malignant perivascular neoplasm is a malignant myopericytoma, a subtype of malignant skin neoplasm. The available immunophenotype is considered diagnostic, and the requested CD34/ERG and PDGFB testing returned no additional data. This further supports the malignant skin neoplasm hypothesis, increasing confidence from 0.98 to 0.99.

Pathological confirmation of a malignant perivascular neoplasm with cellular atypia, mitoses, and necrosis essentially excludes a benign skin neoplasm. The previous clinical impression of a benign vascular or adnexal tumor is overridden by tissue diagnosis, so confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.02.

Pathology demonstrates a malignant perivascular neoplasm with no inflammatory or infectious features. The absence of purulence and the tissue diagnosis make an inflammatory or infectious lesion highly unlikely, reducing confidence from 0.1 to 0.01.

node-7.label: Pathological examination shows a malignant perivascular neoplasm with SMA-positive ovoid cells around vessels, atypia, mitoses, and necrosis

node-8.label: Immunohistochemistry is negative for desmin, calponin, h-caldesmon, and CD31 (endothelial only)

why.why: Pathologist analysis confirms that the SMA-positive perivascular ovoid-cell proliferation with atypia, mitoses, and necrosis, together with negative desmin, calponin, h-caldesmon, and endothelial-only CD31, is diagnostic for malignant myopericytoma. The requested CD34/ERG and PDGFB testing returned no additional data, but the available immunophenotype is sufficient. This expert confirmation raises confidence from 0.85 to 0.96.
